transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-21
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Jordan Rivers (Pinnacle Head of Search), Sam Patel (Pinnacle ML), Anika Bose (Pinnacle PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): quick demo of embeddings + rerank, some questions on dedicated vs hosted, asked for security docs and a pilot benchmark.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, we got about 45 minutes, super excited to walk through a hosted embeddings + rerank flow for your discovery product
[00:15] Jordan: yeah thanks maya, we just want to see how tight the latency is and how much work to swap out our current pipeline, which is a homegrown vector store + a light GBT reranker today
[00:28] Luis: awesome, we'll show a two-stage approach: cheap dense retrieval with embeddings then a lightweight reranker via Redwood hosted endpoint. I'll share the console and quick API call patterns
[00:45] Sam: quick note, our SLA for search is 250ms p95, that's a hard constraint for some of our usecases, others can tolerate up to 500, so curious where hosted sits
[01:02] Maya: good callout, p95 constraints usually drive whether you go dedicated or hosted with burst capacity. Hosted can hit low hundreds for short seqs, depends on model choice and batching. we can show numbers in the benchmark
[01:20] Jordan: and data residency - some logs can't leave region eu-west, is that supported?
[01:29] Luis: yes, we have region routing and optional data residency for hosted; for strict requirements we also offer Private deployments or Dedicated capacity that sits in a customer region. we'll share the docs after
[01:45] Anika: can you walk us through a sample request path? I'm visualizing our flow: user query -> candidate retrieval -> rerank -> serve results
[01:59] Luis: exactly. step 1: call /embeddings endpoint to vectorize queries and the two stage retrieval uses your vector DB. step 2: we call /rerank with doc candidates plus query embedding or raw text. reranker returns scored candidates. you can run rerank with small context windows so latency stays low
[02:25] Maya: i'll pull up the console and a quick curl example now
[02:38] [screen share] Luis: here is the SDK snippet, simple 3 lines: createEmbedding -> top-k retrieval -> rerank endpoint call. We also have an optimize tab that suggests batching sizes and cache TTLs based on request distribution
[03:05] Sam: how does caching work? we have a lot of repeated queries and heavy KV usage currently
[03:15] Luis: we do prefix/KV cache and per-route cache policies. for embeddings we recommend a small LRU cache; for rerank we have a prefix cache that can short-circuit rerank if top candidate confidence is very high. that reduces cost and latency
[03:36] Jordan: hmm, can you give numbers? like if we cache common queries what p95 improvement do you typically see
[03:44] Luis: it depends but we've seen p95 go from ~300-400ms down to ~120-180ms for cached hits on typical retail datasets. for cold paths it stays model-dependent. our Optimize tool estimates token counts and suggests quantization when appropriate
[04:05] Anika: you mentioned quantization, do we need to change our model or is that handled by you?
[04:12] Maya: Redwood recommends quantized model variants for cost-sensitive workloads; it's handled on the serving side — you point to a model variant in config or let Optimize recommend one based on your workload profile
[04:25] Sam: about integration effort: we use Milvus for vector store and have an event pipeline that writes embeddings at ingestion. we want low engineering lift
[04:34] Luis: perfect — typical integration is: you keep your vector store, call the Redwood embeddings endpoint at ingestion or on-demand, store the vector. for rerank the payload is small: doc ids plus snippets. SDKs come with a sample notebook for Milvus. i'll share the notebook link
[04:56] Jordan: ok security — SSO, RBAC, SAML for enterprise admin access? also KMS for keys?
[05:06] Maya: yes we support SAML/SSO, RBAC, org-level controls. For encryption we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations and detailed audit logs for each request. we'll send the SOC2 report and security whitepaper after this call
[05:23] Sam: and retention — can we configure retention and opt out for logs?
[05:29] Luis: yes per-tenant retention policies, and you can opt-out of storing full payloads; there's also token-level obfuscation at rest. we'll include exact fields in the security doc
[05:41] Jordan: what about model regressions — we need quality monitoring
[05:46] Maya: Redwood Optimize includes eval hooks; you can push prompt sets and ground truth, get alerts on quality regression for rerank scores. can tie to rollouts so if a new model degrades we auto-fallback
[06:03] Anika: can you demo the reranker quickly with one of our example queries? we uploaded a sample batch earlier in the shared folder
[06:12] Luis: sure, let's run a live rerank. i'll call the hosted rerank endpoint with sample top-10 candidates. give me a sec
[06:28] [sound of typing, endpoint call executes]
[06:40] Luis: response back in 210ms — that's for a short sequence and small context. here's the returned scores and the top result. you can see how the reranker boosts items with better contextual match
[06:55] Sam: 210ms is promising. what model did you run?
[07:00] Luis: we used a mid-sized open model variant quantized for inference; in hosted you can pick a faster variant or a higher-quality one depending on tradeoffs. we will show benchmark matrix in the results doc
[07:14] Jordan: i saw earlier notes about rate limits — our traffic pattern is spiky, with bursts during peak catalog updates. can Redwood handle bursts without cold starts?
[07:25] Maya: hosted supports burst capacity tiers; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools for predictable capacity. we also have autoscaling for Dedicated with pre-warming options to avoid cold-start latency. for extremely spiky workloads Private or Dedicated is often recommended
[07:44] Anika: cost — ballpark tokens per rerank call? we want to estimate monthly bill for projected 5M searches/month with top-10 rerank
[07:54] Maya: ballpark depends on model and whether you rerank raw text or embeddings + features. i'll include sample math in the pricing doc. as an example: small rerank model might translate to X tokens per request; embeddings have a per-embedding unit. we'll send illustrative spreadsheets
[08:12] Jordan: curious about fallbacks — if capacity is constrained in region, is there automatic fallback to a cheaper model or different region?
[08:21] Luis: yes smart routing with automated fallback policies — you can configure preferred region, then fallback to compatible model variants or to a lower-cost tier so your surface stays up. metrics in console show failover counts
[08:36] Sam: let's talk about the pilot benchmark — how do we run the 10k query test? do you need our logs or sample labels
[08:44] Luis: ideally we get an anonymized sample of queries and their current candidates plus relevance labels if you have them. we'll run on Redwood hosted test workspace with a mirror of your top-k retrieval and then compare rerank MAP/NDCG and latencies. if labels aren't available we can run user-judged evals or simulated heuristics
[09:07] Jordan: we can extract a 10k slice and remove PII. i can have that to you by Friday
[09:14] Maya: perfect — that'll let us produce a comparative report for p95 and cost per 1k queries.
[09:22] Anika: any concerns about vendor lock-in? we want to be able to migrate models later
[09:27] Luis: migration is straightforward — you store your vector DB and have full control of prompt sets. Redwood serves model variants but you can switch to a different provider or a Private deployment; Export of embeddings and logs is supported
[09:40] [brief cross-talk]
[09:50] Sam: small nit — sometimes transcription uses weird names, but unrelated. real question: how often do you recommend retraining or re-indexing embeddings?
[09:59] Luis: depends on content churn; weekly reindex for heavy churn, monthly for stable catalogs. Optimize can recommend cadence based on drift metrics
[10:14] Jordan: ok i'm sold on the approach, but we need cost numbers and security docs to sign off with procurement
[10:21] Maya: we'll send a pricing sheet and SOC2 + security whitepaper. also we can provide an SOW for a 4-week pilot that includes the 10k benchmark and a small integration scope for Milvus
[10:33] Anika: can you include an option for a brief on-prem test? procurement asked about air-gapped options
[10:39] Luis: yes Private/on-prem is an option; we'll include high level steps and dependencies in the SOW
[10:47] [pause as links are pasted into chat]
[10:55] Maya: links: demo notebook (shared), pilot SOW template, security whitepaper, pricing spreadsheet (illustrative). I'll follow up in email with those attachments
[11:07] Jordan: great. next steps — we get the 10k sample to you, you run benchmark, we review results and decide pilot SOW
[11:16] Maya: exactly. recapping action items now
[11:20] [recap] Maya: Jordan to share anonymized logs by 2026-07-24; Maya to send pricing + docs by 2026-07-23; Luis to run 10k rerank benchmark and share results by 2026-07-28
[11:36] Jordan: thanks everyone, that was helpful
[11:40] Anika: thanks y'all
[11:42] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up. bye
